clue.text: Salad without a dressing? That's novel

definitions.text: Salad without a dressing? That's novel

parts.words: Salad without a dressing? That's novel
parts.note: a salad served bare is a midday meal with nothing on it, and that bare meal is also the title of a William Burroughs novel

explanation.surface: Someone serving an undressed salad remarks on the novelty of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like 'new', but it means a book: the bare meal is the title of a Burroughs novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes an undressed midday meal and is also the name of Burroughs's 1959 novel.

clue.text: Finally get you, spineless as usual, inside fight

indicators.note: finally here applies to every following word in the run, taking the closing letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: Someone at last gets to grips with a habitually weak person in a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' seems to modify only 'get', but it takes the last letter of each of the six words from 'get' to 'inside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scuffle or struggle is a fight; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Slip with task

parts.note: to slip is to make a mistake, to err
with means and, joining things together

explanation.surface: A mistake made while doing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A small job someone is sent to do is a task; the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Covering your mess at Rolling Stones

indicators.note: covering means the shuffled letters wrap around the other piece
rolling suggests tumbling, so the letters of mess at are mixed up

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: Someone's mess is being covered up at a Rolling Stones concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stones' reads as the band, but 'Rolling' is the anagram signal and 'Stones' alone is the definition; the shuffle gives AMESTS, which 'Covering' wraps round the old pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethysts are purple gemstones, and stones is the usual jeweller's word for gems.

clue.text: A German follows a German saint, the one Bach composed for opera

indicators.note: follows puts the first a German after the second a German and saint

parts.note: ein is German for a
ein is German for a

indicators.note: composed suggests putting notes in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A German admirer writes an opera for a German saint, the one Bach wrote for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like part of the musical story but signals an anagram of THE ONE BACH, giving ON THE BEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Glass's 1976 work about the physicist is an opera; the title names a specific example of that form.

clue.text: Poor pre-election period, back with a change of heart

indicators.note: the two central letters swap places, so the heart of the word is changed
back means the word for the pre-election period is written backwards

parts.note: purdah is the British term for the period before an election when civil servants avoid new announcements

explanation.surface: A poor pre-election period, followed by a candidate changing their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PURDAH into HADRUP, then 'a change of heart' swaps the middle D and R. Purdah is the UK civil-service quiet period before an election.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of money is being poor; the phrase is an idiom for lacking funds.

clue.text: Good time girl, American one Blairism corrupted

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: corrupted means the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A good-time girl, an American, is one corrupted by Blairism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good time girl' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'time'; 'corrupted' shuffles I and BLAIRISM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means a year of wonders, a remarkably successful period, so a good time.

clue.text: Women's clothing soon to be distributed to soldiers

parts.note: drag is women's clothing worn by a man

indicators.note: distributed means the letters of soon are spread out in a new order

explanation.surface: Women's clothes will soon be handed out to the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Dragoons were mounted infantry, so they are a kind of soldier.

clue.text: A libertine favourite caged bird

indicators.note: caged means one piece is shut inside another

parts.note: a teacher's favourite is the pet
a rake is a dissolute man, a libertine

explanation.surface: A rake's favourite bird is kept in a cage.
explanation.definitionFit: This small long-tailed parrot is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Doctor and nurse go out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor and a nurse leave together.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a medical practitioner, so a doctor in the broad sense.

clue.text: Blonde allegedly gets more of this blonde's pleasure zone

parts.words: Blonde allegedly gets more of this
parts.note: the saying goes that blondes have more fun
fair describes light-coloured hair

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about where a blonde finds pleasure, playing on the saying that blondes have more fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground with rides and stalls is a place of amusement, so a pleasure zone.

clue.text: Lady Godiva's possible cover for honeypot and purse?

definitions.text: Lady Godiva's possible cover for honeypot and purse?

parts.words: Lady Godiva's possible cover for honeypot and purse?
parts.note: Lady Godiva is rhyming slang for a fiver; the naked rider might cover herself with one, and it also goes in a purse

explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang Lady Godiva means a fiver, a British banknote worth five pounds; she rode naked, so a note could cover her modesty.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Godiva rhymes with fiver, the slang name for this banknote, which also fills a purse.

clue.text: See 1
Tax return compiler holds in Devon

indicators.note: return means the tax is written backwards

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
the compiler of the crossword refers to himself as I
a shop's stock is the goods it holds

explanation.surface: A tax-return preparer holds things in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax return' reads as a form, but 'return' reverses VAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tavistock is a market town in Devon, a county in south-west England.

clue.text: Bubbly chap having disturbed siesta, put out

indicators.note: having means the shuffled letters hold the other piece
out means put is knocked out of order along with the jumbled siesta
disturbed means the letters of siesta are jumbled

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man whose nap has been disturbed is annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' reads as annoyed; 'out' merely rounds off the surface. The shuffle gives ASTISPUTE, split by the man after its seventh letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti spumante is an Italian sparkling wine, and bubbly is a casual word for sparkling wine.

clue.text: See 6
The SNP's UK vision unharmed?

definitions.meaning: the Scottish National Party wants Scotland independent, so a liberated Scot
to escape without punishment or injury

explanation.walkthrough: The SNP is the Scottish National Party, which campaigns for Scottish independence from the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting away without penalty or injury is the idiom; the punning reading is an independent Scotland.

clue.text: Indeed, home lost value

indicators.note: in means the home is put inside the deed

parts.note: a flat is a home

explanation.surface: A homeowner confirms that the house has dropped in price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indeed' reads as an affirmation, but the setter splits it as 'In deed', so the container signal and the document come from one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deflated has had its value reduced, as a currency does in deflation.

clue.text: Cook overused ingredients to create masterpieces

parts.note: a cook is a chef

indicators.note: the letters of overused are treated as ingredients, mixed to create something new

explanation.surface: A cook overuses ingredients while trying to make masterpieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for outstanding works is used in English for masterpieces.

clue.text: A final letter in severe danger

indicators.note: in means A and the last letter sit inside the other word

parts.note: hard means harsh or severe
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A last letter warning of serious danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard is a risk or danger; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: A clue to why we hear the conclusion of a fairy tale?

definitions.text: A clue to why we hear the conclusion of a fairy tale?

parts.words: A clue to why we hear the conclusion of a fairy tale?
parts.note: the last letter of happy is Y, pronounced like why, and the phrase also names how fairy tales finish

explanation.walkthrough: Happy ends in Y, which sounds like 'why', so the phrase is a clue to 'why'; it is also how fairy tales close.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy tales traditionally close with everyone living contentedly ever after, the classic upbeat conclusion.

clue.text: Gave information about tree, a crashing bore

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the other letters

parts.note: told means gave information

indicators.note: crashing means tree and a are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone told a story about a tree, a crashing bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a noun after 'crashing', but it is the past tense of bear; 'crashing' makes ERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore here is the past tense of bear, meaning put up with, so tolerated.

clue.text: Handle, say, a new car dispute

definitions.meaning: to drive a new car gently through its first miles

explanation.walkthrough: Running in a new engine means driving it gently at first; a quarrel is a separate sense of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a careful early drive of a new car and a quarrel are senses of the phrasal noun.

clue.text: See 4
Get back together with leader at the end backing train

indicators.note: backing means the result is written backwards
the first letter is moved to the end of the word

parts.note: to reunite is to get back together

explanation.surface: A couple reunite, with their leader bringing up the rear of the train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with leader at the end' moves R to the end, giving EUNITER, and 'backing' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a train of attendants following an important person.

clue.text: Light palm product (twice)

parts.note: palm oil is a product of the palm

indicators.note: product, read a second time, means the result of working the letters of palm into a new order

explanation.surface: A light made from palm products, used twice.
explanation.walkthrough: '(twice)' tells the solver to read 'palm product' twice: once as OIL, once as an anagram of PALM.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil lamp is a lamp burning oil, so a source of light.

clue.text: See 19
Perhaps safety poster held back an annual celebration

indicators.note: held means the reversed poster is enclosed inside
perhaps indicates a possible rearrangement of the letters of safety
back means the poster is turned around

parts.note: an advertisement, AD

explanation.surface: Perhaps a safety poster is held back for a yearly celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' makes FEASTY, and 'back' gives DA, which 'held' places before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast day is a yearly religious festival, so a celebration held annually.
